name: Escitalopram + Etizolam
meta: Schedule H – prescription only; Etizolam: Schedule H – prescription only; regulated as a controlled psychotropic in several states (verify current notification)
sections: Fine white to slightly yellow powder (oxalate), sparingly soluble in water.
White to pale yellowish crystalline powder.

Escitalopram Oxalate: The therapeutically active S-enantiomer of citalopram; approved for major depression in 2002 and generalised anxiety disorder in 2003. First approval/introduction: US FDA August 2002 (Lundbeck / Forest Laboratories). Etizolam: A thienotriazolodiazepine marketed in Japan, Italy and India; not approved in the USA or UK. First approval/introduction: Patented 1972; approved in Japan 1984 (Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical).
Etizolam (thienodiazepine) gives rapid anxiolysis while escitalopram takes effect; combination improves early symptom control and adherence. Dependence potential requires short-term use.

Escitalopram Oxalate S-enantiomer of citalopram; the most selective SSRI. Inhibits serotonin reuptake at the presynaptic transporter, with allosteric binding that prolongs transporter blockade. Receptor / target profile: The most SERT-selective SSRI, binding both orthosteric and allosteric sites (Ki 0.8–1.1 nM); negligible NET/DAT activity.

Etizolam Agonist at the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors, producing anxiolytic, hypnotic, muscle-relaxant and anticonvulsant effects; potency ~6–10 times diazepam. Receptor / target profile: Positive allosteric modulator at the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors; clinically regarded as a benzodiazepine.
Summary: Bioavailability ~80%; Tmax ~4 h. ~56% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C19, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Half-life ~27–32 h.
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax 0.5–2 h. Metabolised by CYP3A4 to active alpha-hydroxyetizolam. Half-life ~3.4 h (metabolite ~8 h).

Escitalopram Oxalate: QTc in patients with cardiac risk; sodium in elderly; mood/suicidality during first weeks.

Escitalopram Oxalate: Dizziness, tremor, agitation, somnolence, seizures, QT prolongation, serotonin syndrome. Supportive care with ECG monitoring. Etizolam: Somnolence, ataxia, respiratory depression, coma. Supportive care; flumazenil with caution.
Evidence derives from component trials; short-term benzodiazepine co-initiation speeds early anxiolysis with SSRIs (Goddard 2001 by analogy).
Initial anxiety or nausea may occur – usually temporary
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
